newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds down on nervousness over weak punt/stg.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds down on nervousness over weak punt/stg.

text.p: Irish bonds were down in nervous trade late on Thursday, hit by worries about the Irish pound's continued weakness against sterling, dealers said.

"Irish bonds have had a down day. The fact that the Irish pound is trading below 1.01 stg has caused confusion regarding Ireland's monetary policy in the run up to European Monetary Union (EMU)," one dealer said.

"A lot of sellers have come in to the Irish market as a result and we are now trading 93 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area while we are trading 70 through (below) the UK," the dealer added.
By 1525 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had eased 15p from to 106.30 to yield 6.09 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 also eased 15p to 107.15 to yield 6.85 percent.
The Irish pound was at 1.0080 sterling compared with 1.0117 sterling at Wednesday's close.

Dealers said a close eye is likely to be kept on international markets amid news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had fired his security chief, Alexander Lebed. -- Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 6603377
